# AI Gateway for DeepSeek Harness
English | 简体中文
Connect **any AI gateway** to DeepSeek Harness — chat over OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini protocols, wi
th models, parameters and quota in one place.
Most providers are the same three endpoints with different names on the box. Instead of a list of su
pported vendors, this plugin follows the protocol and probes each gateway for what it can actually d
o: if it speaks `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`, it works — including a gateway nobody has h
aks `/v1/models` and `/v1/chat/completions`, it works — including a gateway nobody has heard of yet.

## What it does
- **Probe before saving.** A gateway is written only after it lists its models with the address and
token you entered. A wrong URL or a revoked token is refused at that moment, not on the first messag

e.
- **Several gateways at once.** Every saved gateway gets its own provider route and stays usable;
the chat model picker groups them by gateway name, so two gateways serving the same model id never

collide.
- **Model management per gateway.** Fetch the gateway's list, add a model it does not list,
edit any model's name, upstream mapping, context window, output cap, input modalities, reasoning le

vels and wire protocol, and hide what you do not want.
- **Grouped model table.** Models are grouped
by vendor — `devin/claude-opus-5` and `claude-opus-5-5` sit together under Anthropic — with a per-g

roup "tested / working" count. Groups collapse, and the grouping can be switched off.
- **Hide model
s.** Hide one model, or a whole vendor group, from the chat picker without removing it; Hidden model
s stay in the list, greyed out, so clicking again unhides them. Hiding never turns an automatic gate

way into a fixed list.
- **Shelve a gateway.** The eye button on a gateway card hides that one gatew
ay from the conversation picker while its address, token, model settings and history resolution stay

intact.
- **Model tests.** Test one model or a batch: one tiny request each, bounded output, errors

classified (no upstream channel, invalid token, rate limited, timed out).
- **Quota where it exists
, silence where it does not.** New API, LiteLLM and one-api-family backends report quota; every othe

r gateway simply shows no quota instead of an error.
- **The gateway's own identity.** The channel s
hows the site's favicon when it has one, its declared name (page title, then the backend's own name)
, its version, chat protocols and public facts. Unknown gateways fall back to a neutral icon.
## Supported backends
The plugin never needs to recognise a vendor — recognition only decides the icon and which quota end
er needs to recognise a vendor — recognition only decides the icon and which quota endpoint to call.
| Backend | Detected by | Quota |
| New API / one-api / done-hub / one-hub / Veloera / VoAPI | `GET /api/status` (`system_name`, `quot

a_per_unit`) | `GET /api/usage/token/` |
| LiteLLM | `GET /key/info` answering | key budget (`spend`

/ `max_budget`) |
| CLIProxyAPI | `GET /` banner `CLI Proxy API Server` | none |
| Anything else th
at is OpenAI-compatible | `GET /v1/models` answering | none |
Wire protocols per model: OpenAI Chat Completions, OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, Gemini. The
gateway's `supported_endpoint_types` decides; the model editor can override.
## Several gateways, one picker
Each saved gateway is registered as its own provider route, so every gateway is usable at the same t
ime — there is nothing to switch between. The model picker groups models by gateway, and the group h
eading is the gateway's name: two gateways serving the same model id appear as separate rows instead
of one shadowing the other.

## Model capabilities and controls
**Sync data** reloads the currently viewed gateway's model capabilities even when no settings change
d. **Fetch models** also refreshes that gateway's capabilities after discovery, including in automat
ic mode when every discovered model is already enabled. Neither action requires reopening settings;
periodic background snapshots still do not fetch model catalogs.
Fetching a model list also resolves per-model reasoning levels and speed tiers. Reasoning resolution
prefers manual mappings, then gateway `supported_reasoning_levels` / `default_reasoning_level`, the
n pi-ai's bundled catalog or family defaults. Those fallbacks are model metadata, **not gateway decl
arations**; unrecognised support remains unknown. `supports_reasoning_effort_updates` only says whet
her a running turn may change its level (Claude answers `false`), so it never blanks the level selec
tor. A resolved model also keeps pi-ai's own `compat` block for that id (for example `forceAdaptiveT
hinking`), so a level reaches the upstream as an adaptive effort rather than a thinking-token budget
. Only per-model `service_tiers` / `supported_service_tiers` establish speed declarations. Discovery
never sends billed model probes.
The model editor has independent reasoning and speed switches, with row-based add/remove controls an
d editable API values. Turning speed off hides the composer control and omits `service_tier`, includ
ing old conversation choices. Turning reasoning selection off removes its level menu. Detection meta
data is retained for re-enabling.
## Privacy and safety

- Requests are read-only `GET`s; **no model is called and nothing is billed** by probing.
- Redirect

s are never followed, so a token cannot be forwarded to another host.
- Site icons are fetched only

from the gateway's own origin, size-limited, and cached on disk for 24 hours.
- Identification uses
only public endpoints and stores only public facts (family, version, title, icon) — no token, no use

r data.
- A gateway without a quota endpoint is reported as having none, never as an error.
